verdict.rationale: The Gemini API documents a broad programmatic surface: text, image and media generation, multimodal input, Live API, Batch API, embeddings, function calling, safety settings, webhooks and a CLI. Supervised tuning jobs can be created via the console, REST and the SDK alike, which is one concrete case of UI/API parity. However, nothing states general parity with the AI Studio UI, and at least one capability (viewing active rate limits) is pointed to AI Studio rather than an API. Missing for 10: an explicit UI/API parity statement, API access to UI-only items like rate-limit visibility, and independent hands-on confirmation of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: explore text generation, multimodal understanding, image generation, structured output, tools, function calling, agents, and background execution
The page documents creating tuning jobs via console, REST, and the Google Gen AI SDK.
The Gemini Batch API is designed to process large volumes of requests asynchronously at 50% of the standard cost.
The Gemini API CLI (`gemini-api`) is a stateless, zero-dependency command-line client built for AI agents with shell access, scripts, and CI pipelines.
